evidence: Varr. LL 5.136: homō in prātīs per fēnisecia eō festūcās corrādit
terms.comment: Varro’s verb for raking up the stalks after haymaking, and his account of the name of the rake: ab rāsū rāstellī dictī (rightly, from rādō). Rare, and mostly ante- and post-classical (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: Folia rāstellō corrādāmus, deinde in acervum congerēmus.
phrases.english: Let’s rake up the leaves, then we’ll pile them in a heap.

phrases.latin: itaque homō in prātīs per fēnisecia eō festūcās corrādit, quō ab rāsū rāstellī dictī
phrases.english: so in the meadows at haymaking a man rakes up the stalks with it, and from this scraping rakes are called rāstellī

rastellus.html: The inherited quantity follows the rāstrum family.

sources: Lewis & Short: corrado · Lewis & Short: festuca
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 368.
